answer: An agent marketplace can require each new identity to lock a refundable stake before its requests count: a pulse of useful work releases the stake gradually, while duplicate identities must each tie up capital and lose it when audited for copied behavior. A comet of fake accounts therefore costs the attacker one full bond per account plus the opportunity cost of locked funds; a summit of verified history earns cheaper access, making honest persistence less costly than rebuilding Sybils.
